sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
kicker: Value commerce · parcels vs revenue at listed carriers
title: Parcels got cheaper. Meesho's margin rose.
dek: Three listed carriers handled 31–70% more parcels but grew revenue only 20–57%; Meesho cut its logistics cost by about ₹4 an order and lifted contribution margin to about 6% of NMV.

chart.title: Parcels handled vs revenue, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: growth as stated on Q2 calls · Shiprocket: core shipping arm · Shadowfax, Delhivery: total revenue

stats.label: Lower logistics cost per Meesho order
stats.note: Fewer returns, denser routes, a new middle mile; contribution margin ≈6% of NMV vs 4%.

stats.label: Shiprocket's core yield
stats.note: Core shipments +31%, core revenue +25%, on customer mix and lower-yield hyperlocal orders.

stats.label: Meesho adjusted EBITDA, of NMV
stats.note: Still loss-making (Q2 net loss ₹132 cr), and part of the saving goes back in price.

read: Cheaper parcels are reaching the platform's margin first; the Q3 festive print will show whether Meesho keeps ≈6% or hands it back in price.
notes: Volume and revenue growth are year-on-year figures given on the Q2 FY27 calls: Shadowfax orders delivered (+70%) vs total revenue (+57%), Delhivery shipments (+32%) vs consolidated revenue (+20%, filed), Shiprocket core-shipping transactions (+31%) vs core revenue (+25%). Delhivery's and Shadowfax's revenue also include freight, hyperlocal and other services, so the gap is an indicator of falling revenue per parcel, not a measured yield; Shiprocket quantified its core yield fall at 4–5%. Meesho's ≈₹4 per-order saving (Q2 vs Q1) and ≈6% contribution margin are from its Q2 call; the 4% comparison is its Q4 FY26 exit rate. Meesho, Shadowfax and Shiprocket are recent listings, so filed year-ago results are not on the desk.
